findings.evidence: grep for `ofReal` in the file returns no hit inside lines 11-82 (the module docstring); first hit is line 102 in `trialLaw`. The sibling file does state it: `Uniform/Basic.lean:107` "`min (a x) 1`, read as `0` where `a x` is negative".
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the module docstring: densities are read through `ENNReal.ofReal`, so negative values of `f` and `g` count as `0` and "`f` normalised" means the positive part of `f` normalised. Write `μ.withDensity (ENNReal.ofReal ∘ g)` on line 20.
findings.issue: The module docstring never records the `ENNReal.ofReal` convention (the PR description claims it does). It says the trial law is "the product of the proposal law `μ.withDensity g`" (line 20), which is not the definition — `trialLaw` uses `μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (g x)` (line 102) — and the Main-results entries say the accepted law is "`min f (c * g)` normalised" / "`f` normalised" (lines 37-44). For `f` or `g` with negative values these are the positive parts, so "f normalised" is not what the theorems give. Only `trialLaw`'s own docstring (line 99) states the convention, and only for `g`.

findings.evidence: Lines 178-179, 214-215, 240-241 all wrap the density in `ENNReal.ofReal`, while the docstrings at 173-175, 211-212, 236-237 name the bare real function and stress the absence of a sign hypothesis.
findings.fix: In each of the three docstrings say the density is read through `ENNReal.ofReal`, i.e. the negative part of `f` (and of `c * g`) contributes `0` — e.g. "density `ENNReal.ofReal (min f (c * g) / c)`, so negative values contribute `0`".
findings.issue: Same elision where it is most misleading: `map_fst_restrict_trialLaw_acceptSet` is documented as "the measure `μ` with density `min f (c * g) / c`" and "No bound and no sign hypothesis on `f` or `g` is needed", but the statement's density is `ENNReal.ofReal (min (f x) (c * g x) / c)`, i.e. clipped at `0` exactly in the unsigned case the sentence advertises. Same pairing in `acceptedLaw_eq_smul_withDensity_min` (line 211, "the law `min f (c * g)` normalised against `μ`", "whatever the relation between `f` and `c * g`") and `acceptedLaw_eq_smul_withDensity_of_ae_le` (line 236, "the accepted variate has the law `f` normalised").

summary: Documentation is otherwise accurate and the examples check out, but AcceptReject.lean's module docstring and three headline docstrings describe the results in terms of `f` and `g` themselves while every statement reads densities through `ENNReal.ofReal`; combined with the repeated "no sign hypothesis" claim this promises more than the theorems deliver.
